understandingEvidence.essentialUnderstandingDe: Für dieselben Körper in einem gemeinsamen Inertialsystem entspricht die Änderung ihres Gesamtimpulsvektors dem resultierenden äußeren Kraftstoß. Ist dieser über das betrachtete Intervall null, sind die Gesamtimpulse an den beiden Endpunkten gleich. Beim gegenseitigen Abstoßen können sich die Einzelimpulse dennoch ändern.
understandingEvidence.essentialUnderstandingEn: For the same bodies in one common inertial frame, the change in their total momentum vector equals the net external impulse. If that impulse is zero over the interval, the total momenta at its endpoints are equal. The individual momenta can still change as the bodies push apart.
understandingEvidence.observablePerformanceDe: Für zwei anfangs ruhende, unterschiedlich schwere Wagen auf einer horizontalen reibungsarmen Bahn benennt die lernende Person das System aus Wagen und Feder und wählt im Bezugssystem der Bahn eine positive Richtung. Sie begründet, warum der äußere horizontale Kraftstoß und der Impuls der leichten Feder beim kurzen Abstoß vernachlässigbar sind. Aus der gerichteten Bilanz erklärt sie selbstständig, warum die Wagen entgegengesetzte, annähernd gleich große Impulse haben und der leichtere Wagen im Modell schneller ist.
understandingEvidence.observablePerformanceEn: For two unequal-mass carts initially at rest on a horizontal low-friction track, the learner identifies the carts and spring as the system and chooses a positive direction in the track frame. They justify neglecting the external horizontal impulse and the light spring’s momentum during the brief push. Using the signed balance, they independently explain why the carts have opposite momenta of nearly equal magnitude and why the lighter cart is faster in the model.
understandingEvidence.transferExpectationDe: In einer neuen Aufgabe driften eine Astronautin und ein Paket gemeinsam nach rechts. Nimmt der Rechtsimpuls des Pakets beim Abstoßen zu und ist der äußere Kraftstoß vernachlässigbar, begründet die lernende Person die nach links gerichtete Impulsänderung der Astronautin. Durch Vergleich mit deren anfänglichem Rechtsimpuls erklärt sie, wann die Astronautin weiter nach rechts fliegt, zum Stillstand kommt oder sich nach links bewegt.
understandingEvidence.transferExpectationEn: In a fresh task, an astronaut and a package initially drift together to the right. When the push increases the package’s rightward momentum and the external impulse is negligible, the learner justifies the astronaut’s leftward momentum change. By comparing that change with her initial rightward momentum, they explain when she continues to the right, comes to rest, or moves to the left.

descriptionReviews.rationale: Both versions make the same testable claim about the same bodies in one inertial frame. Zero net external impulse over the specified interval justifies equating the two endpoint vectors, even if external forces acted in between. Using that equality to explain recoil gives the learner a concrete qualitative performance without requiring a derivation or a numerical inversion.

profileReviews.reason: The DE and EN expectations give exact endpoint equality for zero net external impulse and use approximate equality when an external impulse is merely negligible. In the astronaut case the same astronaut and package are compared in one inertial frame. The package gains rightward momentum, so the astronaut’s change is approximately equal and leftward. All three stated final directions of motion, including rest as the zero-velocity case, are accounted for by comparing the change with her initial momentum. In the cart case both carts and the negligible-mass spring belong to the system in the track frame. The level, low-friction track justifies neglecting external horizontal impulse during release, and the spring model permits neglecting its own momentum. The signed cart momenta then approximately cancel, with the lighter cart faster in the model. No exact measured equality or speed-ratio calculation is required. The two briefs vary the initial total momentum and call for independent explanations in both languages.

cardReviews.scientificCorrectness: For a fixed material system in one inertial frame, zero net external impulse implies P(t₂) = P(t₁). External impulses at different times can cancel while P varies in between. Zero net external force throughout the interval gives continuous constancy.
cardReviews.languageEquivalence: Both variants define total momentum as the vector sum and give the same system, frame, interval implication and throughout-force condition.
cardReviews.originFit: Both variants name only 839ecc8f-3a60-418b-bc92-64bfeef33824. The endpoint balance directly supports its recoil explanation, and the continuous case clarifies the limit of that balance.
cardReviews.promptAnswerFit: Both fronts ask about endpoint equality and continuous conservation. Each back answers both parts and explicitly limits what follows from zero net impulse.
cardReviews.recallBoundary: Reciting the two conditions demonstrates recall. The goal also requires choosing the bodies and using the vector balance to justify a recoil prediction independently.

cardReviews.scientificCorrectness: For the same material system in an inertial frame, dP/dt equals the vector sum of external forces. If that sum vanishes throughout the interval, P is constant throughout.
cardReviews.languageEquivalence: The German and English variants specify the same material closure, inertial frame, vector differential balance and force condition.

cardReviews.promptAnswerFit: Each front asks for momentum balance with external forces. The differential equation answers it directly, and the final sentence gives its zero-force consequence.
